title: Nur al-Din Ali of Damascus and the Damsel Sitt al-Milah (ಕನ್ನಡ)

keywords: nur al-din ali of damascus and the damsel sitt al-milah
full_text:
Nur al-Din Ali was a refined young silk merchant of Damascus, renowned for his graceful manners and love of literature. He loved Sitt al-Milah, daughter of an affluent judge, whose poetic mastery was celebrated across the city.

Instead of forward approaches, Nur al-Din sent her an exquisite illuminated manuscript of classical love poetry, accompanied by a modest letter seeking permission to court her with honorable intentions.

Sitt al-Milah replied with an original poem inscribed upon rose-tinted parchment, testing his understanding of the classical meters and the ethical duties of companionship.

For six months, they conducted an intellectual correspondence of breathtaking elegance, discussing history, ethics, and art, until their mutual respect blossomed into deep love.

When Nur al-Din approached the judge to ask for her hand, the judge was astonished: 'You have courted my daughter with the refinement of ancient poets, without a single breath of scandal!'

The marriage was celebrated with thirty days of music in Damascus, proving that true courtship is a dialogue of minds and souls.
moral: Mutual respect, poetic correspondence, and honorable intentions create an enduring marriage. [KN]
